harmbench: A public framework for standardized red-team and refusal evaluation.
simpleqa: Public evaluation implementations, including SimpleQA. Pin the specific task and grader revision.
webarena: Browser-agent tasks in reproducible web environments.
belebele: Multilingual reading-comprehension data and evaluation resources.
sklearn-metrics: Definitions and implementation details for prediction metrics. Check the convention used by your installed version.
sklearn-cv: Cross-validation designs, group-aware splitting, and time-series splitting.
judge-paper: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
A primary study of model judges, preference evaluation, and evaluator biases.
longbench: Long-context benchmark versions and evaluation code.
mmmu: Multidisciplinary multimodal understanding and reasoning tasks.
whisper: Speech-recognition research and evaluation context. Follow language and text-normalization conventions.
fairlearn: Disaggregated metrics, group comparisons, and interpretation of fairness measures.
mlperf: Performance scenarios with defined workloads and quality constraints. Official rules govern compliant submissions.
vllm: Model serving and inference implementation. Consult its matching version for serving and benchmark commands.
harness-cli: The documented run, ls, and validate subcommands used in the public-benchmark walkthrough.
inspect: Framework components for model and agent evaluations.
promptfoo: Declarative testing and comparisons for prompts and AI applications.
ifeval: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
Verifiable instruction-following constraints and their evaluation.
mmlu-pro: A separate benchmark with revised and more challenging multiple-choice tasks.
evalplus: Expanded executable tests for supported code-generation benchmarks.
livecode: Time-based code evaluation. State the release and date window used.
tau2: Tool-agent-user interaction with domain-specific tasks and environments.
tinybenchmarks: tinyBenchmarks: evaluating LLMs with fewer examples
A primary study of smaller benchmark sets and item-response-based estimation. Its assumptions and validation matter.
kappa: Agreement statistic, implementation, and inference details.
coco: Official detection metric conventions and thresholds.

glossary.Estimand: The precise quantity an experiment aims to estimate for a specified population and set of conditions.
glossary.Cross-validation: Repeated fitting and evaluation on planned training and held-out partitions of a dataset.
glossary.Nested cross-validation: A design with inner folds for model selection and outer folds for evaluating that selection process.
glossary.Power: The probability that an analysis detects a specified effect when that effect exists, under its assumptions.
glossary.Construct validity: Whether evidence supports interpreting a test as a measurement of its intended ability or property.
glossary.Item response theory: A family of models relating responses to item properties and latent ability estimates under explicit assumptions.
glossary.Time to first token: The elapsed time to the first generated token under a stated timing boundary.
glossary.Inter-token latency: The elapsed time between successive output tokens under a stated measurement convention.
glossary.Prefill: The inference stage that processes the input context before token-by-token generation.
glossary.KV cache: Stored key and value representations reused by attention during autoregressive generation.
glossary.Pareto frontier: Configurations for which improving one measured objective requires worsening at least one other objective.
glossary.Word error rate: The sum of word substitutions, deletions, and insertions divided by the reference word count.
glossary.Intersection over union: The overlap of two regions divided by their union under the selected region definition.
glossary.Oracle context: Correct evidence supplied directly to a system to separate retrieval failures from later failures.
glossary.Cohen's kappa: A chance-corrected agreement measure for two raters with a specified label scheme.
glossary.Bradley–Terry model: A probabilistic model of pairwise outcomes using relative strength parameters.
glossary.Goodhart's law: A warning that optimizing a proxy measure can weaken its relationship with the actual objective.
glossary.Demographic parity: A criterion comparing positive-decision rates across specified groups.
glossary.Equalized odds: A criterion comparing error rates across specified groups conditional on the true outcome.
